newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $5 lower Monday as traders expect to see some follow-through selling on the heels of Friday's downturn.

New York cocoa futures ended lower Friday in a technical correction to Thursday's rally to six-week highs. July cocoa finished down $14 at $1,467 a tonne after trading from $1,490 to $1,446. Second-month September slipped the same to $1,493, while the remaining months slumped $14 to $18.
Technically, traders said July key support was pegged at $1,445-$1,441, while the $1,494-$1,501 chart gap was still seen as a critical resistance level.

London cocoa futures were firmer early Monday, in thin, rangebound dealings with many Europeans countries on public holiday. LIFFE July cocoa was up four stg at the midday break, to 1,020 stg, after ranging from 1,021 to 1,018 stg. Sepember was up three stg, to 1,037 stg. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk 212 859 1640))
